title: Rama Waits Out the Rains
hook: Rama, with every reason to rush, waits out the rains before the search for Sita: the Hindu year has seasons for waiting and for setting out
carry: the hindu year has a season for waiting
tomorrow: why did Bhishma wait for the sun?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vishvamitra woke Rama at dawn: Hindus keep the day's joints with prayer.

Rama has found an ally at last. Sugriva, the monkey king, has promised to send his armies to search for Sita. Then the sky turns. Clouds pile over the mountains, the rivers swell, the roads turn to mud. Rama, whose wife has been carried off, has to sit on a mountainside and wait. Four months.
screen: `AN ALLY, AT LAST.` → `THEN THE RAINS.` → `RAMA WAITS FOUR MONTHS.`

segments.voice: In the Kishkindha book of Valmiki's Ramayana, Rama makes the call himself. The rainy months have begun, he tells Sugriva; this is no time to march. Go home to your city, and when the month of Kartika comes, after the rains, make ready. Then he spends the season in a cave on Mount Prasravana, watching the storms and aching for Sita, and the poet gives that waiting some of his loveliest verses. When the clear autumn sky comes, sharad, and Lakshmana gives a forgetful Sugriva a sharp reminder, the search begins. Here's the teaching. Hindu life keeps step with the year, and the year has seasons for waiting and seasons for going. Many Hindus still keep chaturmas, the four months of the rains, when Vishnu is said to sleep on the cosmic serpent. Wandering monks traditionally stop traveling and stay in one place. Many families hold no weddings until Vishnu wakes, on Prabodhini Ekadashi, in Kartika, the same month Rama waited for. Ayurveda reads the year the same way: ritucharya, the conduct of the season, a twin of the daily routine. The Ashtanga Hridaya counts six seasons, the rains among them, and the Charaka Samhita says a person who knows what suits each season, in food and in activity, grows in strength. Today, that's a different way to see a delay. Not every pause is a failure. In the Hindu year, some seasons are for staying put and gathering strength, and some are for setting out. Rama, with every reason to rush, waited for his season.
screen: `RAMA WAITS ON MOUNT PRASRAVANA` · `AUTUMN COMES, THE SEARCH BEGINS` · `CHATURMAS AND RITUCHARYA` · `A SEASON FOR WAITING, A SEASON FOR GOING`

segments.voice: Notice the air on your skin, warm or cool, damp or dry, and the light where you are. Then turn inward: is this a season in your life for staying put, or for setting out? No fixing, just a weather report from the inside. If you pray, you can offer the season you're in; many Hindus would say a name of Vishnu, like Om Namo Narayanaya.
The seasons. Ritu, a season, and ritucharya, the conduct that keeps step with it, from the rains to the clear autumn when Rama set out.
Your line: the Hindu year has a season for waiting. Rama waited out the rains. Back tomorrow, same hill.
